content: The BIS Patna Branch Laboratory (PBL) is located at Patliputra Industrial Estate, Patna, Bihar - 800013. Contact: pbol@bis.gov.in; telephone 0612-2262808 / +91 6201317797.

title: BIS, Guwahati Branch Laboratory (GBL)
content: The BIS Guwahati Branch Laboratory (GBL) is located at 2nd Floor, West End Block, Housefed Building Complex, Last Gate, Dispur, Guwahati, Assam - 781006. Contact: gbol@bis.gov.in; telephone +91 361 2224670 / +91 9641193329.

title: BIS, Hyderabad Branch Laboratory (HYBL)
content: The BIS Hyderabad Branch Laboratory (HYBL) is located at Plot no. 1, Sy no. 367/1, Moula Ali, Hyderabad - 500040, Telangana. Details of scope and testing capability at this laboratory are published on the BIS LIMS portal along with the laboratory's contact information.

title: BIS Laboratory FAQ - Indian-Standard-wise list of recognized laboratories
content: An Indian-Standard-wise list of laboratories recognized by BIS, usable for BIS conformity-assessment testing purposes, is available on the LIMS portal (lims.bis.gov.in). BIS uses test facilities in its own 8 laboratories, Group-1 laboratories recognized under the Laboratory Recognition Scheme, and Group-2 government laboratories empanelled by BIS.

title: BIS Laboratory FAQ - application process for laboratory recognition
content: A laboratory desiring BIS recognition or empanelment must submit its application online through the LIMS portal (lims.bis.gov.in); detailed steps are provided in the User Manual available on the portal. The fee structure for laboratory recognition is set out in the Laboratory Recognition Scheme document and its subsequent amendments.

title: BIS Laboratory FAQ - no commercial testing by BIS labs
content: BIS laboratories only test products for the purposes of BIS's own Conformity Assessment Schemes and do not carry out commercial testing for the general public. For commercial testing needs, the services of BIS-recognized/empanelled laboratories, as well as other outside laboratories, can be utilized instead.

title: BIS Laboratory FAQ - sample submission via Manakonline
content: Product samples can be sent to BIS laboratories only after a test request is generated through the BIS Manakonline portal (manakonline.in). If a laboratory does not complete testing within an adequate timeframe, the details of the sample and the laboratory may be escalated/communicated to BIS for follow-up.

title: Unified Test Report Formats (UTRFs) for CRS products
content: BIS publishes Unified Test Report Formats (UTRFs) for products covered under the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS), standardizing the format in which BIS-recognized laboratories report test results for CRS-covered electronic and IT goods, to support consistency and ease of review across different testing laboratories.

title: Laboratory Services contact - Laboratory Policy & Planning / Laboratory Recognition & Management Departments
content: Enquiries relating to BIS laboratory services can be directed to the Laboratory Policy and Planning Department or the Laboratory Recognition and Management Department, Room No. 312, Manak Bhawan, Bureau of Indian Standards, 9 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi - 110002; telephone +91 11 23232932 / 23238531; email lppd[at]bis[dot]gov[dot]in or lrmd-bis[at]bis[dot]gov[dot]in.

title: BIS Care mobile app - overview
content: BIS Care is BIS's official mobile app, launched to let consumers check the authenticity of ISI-marked, hallmarked, and CRS-registration-marked products, and to lodge complaints. The app was launched along with three e-BIS portals (Standardization, Conformity Assessment, and Training) on manakonline.in by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution. It is available for both Android and iOS users and is free to download.

title: BIS Care app - verification and complaint features
content: The BIS Care app lets a user enter a licence number, HUID number, or registration number appearing on a product to retrieve details such as the manufacturer's name and address, validity of the licence/registration, the varieties/brands covered, and (for jewellery) the purity of the article. The app's 'Complaints' feature lets users register grievances about poor or sub-standard quality of marked products, misuse of BIS marks, misleading quality claims, or service lapses, through a simple registration/OTP-based login, and provides an acknowledgement with a complaint number for tracking.

title: BIS Care app - language support and registration
content: The BIS Care app supports 12 languages (10 regional languages, plus Hindi and English). A consumer registers through a simplified one-time registration process, entering name and mobile number (with an option to provide an email ID), and can use the app after email verification via a One Time Password (OTP).
source_name: Bureau of Indian Standards (via Vikaspedia, Government of India portal)

title: Online Complaint Registration portal
content: BIS provides an online Complaint Registration facility on its website (in addition to the BIS Care app) where consumers can lodge complaints regarding sub-standard quality of ISI-marked, hallmarked, or CRS-registered products, misuse of BIS's marks, or misleading quality claims, for investigation and redressal by BIS's Complaints Management and Enforcement Department.

title: BIS Citizen's Charter
content: BIS publishes a Citizen's Charter on its website, setting out its service commitments, standards of service delivery, and grievance-redressal mechanisms for stakeholders including manufacturers, jewellers, laboratories, and consumers who interact with BIS's certification, hallmarking, and standardization functions.

title: Standards Clubs programme - overview and objective
content: BIS implements the Standards Clubs programme in schools and colleges across the country, with the objective of sensitizing young members of society about the importance of standards in improving quality of life. Standards Clubs can be formed in any educational institution in India - high and higher-secondary schools, engineering colleges, science colleges, polytechnics, and other professional institutions.

title: Standards Clubs - eligibility and formation requirements
content: Students of class IX and above studying science subjects (or pursuing science/engineering degree/diploma courses) are eligible to be Standards Club members. A club must have a Mentor (one science teacher for classes IX-XII, or a lecturer or above for science/engineering subjects) and a minimum of 15 student members. Consumer Organizations, NGOs, or Voluntary Organizations registered on BIS's Consumer Engagement Portal can facilitate club formation/functioning outside engineering institutions.

title: Standards Clubs - financial support and grants
content: Financial support for Standards Clubs in Engineering Institutions is up to Rs 100,000 per year (subject to organizing at least two activities per year); for institutions other than Engineering Institutions, up to Rs 10,000 per activity (maximum three activities per year). Eligible high/higher-secondary Government Schools with Standards Clubs may receive a one-time Laboratory Grant of up to Rs 50,000 for upgrading science labs, and financial assistance of up to Rs 1,00,000 to establish a 'Manak Kaksha' (Standards Room) with amenities like smart TVs and audio-video systems.
source_name: Bureau of Indian Standards (via Vikaspedia, Government of India portal)

title: Standards Clubs - activities and quality-awareness programmes
content: Standards Clubs organize activities such as orientation programmes on standardization and consumer awareness, industrial visits, quiz/essay-writing/debate competitions on the quality-and-standards ecosystem, and 'Quality Pledge' and 'Quality Connect' events, aimed at cultivating what BIS terms future 'quality ambassadors' among students.

title: Standards Clubs - scale of the programme
content: As of September 2023, BIS had established 6,467 Standards Clubs in schools and colleges across the country - 5,562 in schools and 905 in colleges, of which 384 clubs were in engineering colleges. BIS's engagement with academic institutions on this programme began in December 2020.
source_name: Bureau of Indian Standards (via All India Radio/Prasar Bharati)

title: Consumer Organizations/NGOs engagement in Standards Clubs
content: A Consumer Group or NGO wishing to participate in the formation or operation of Standards Clubs must be registered with NGO Darpan (NITI Aayog) and subsequently with BIS's Consumer Engagement Portal, and must have experience working in the education sector or in the promotion of science and technology. Applications for participation are submitted online through the Consumer Engagement Portal.

title: BIS training activities - National Institute of Training for Standardization (NITS)
content: BIS conducts training programmes on standardization, conformity assessment, and quality management through its training wing, formalized as the National Institute of Training for Standardization (NITS), offering courses aimed at industry professionals, government officials, students, and other stakeholders on topics related to Indian and international standards.

title: BIS enforcement activities
content: BIS's enforcement function covers surveillance of the market and of licensed/registered entities to detect misuse of the Standard Mark (including the ISI mark and Hallmark), sale of non-conforming or spurious goods, and non-compliant advertising, working alongside its Complaints Management and Enforcement Department to investigate and act on complaints and surveillance findings.

title: BIS's role in Government e-Marketplace and public procurement quality assurance
content: BIS supports quality assurance in public procurement by maintaining the Standard Mark and certification/registration ecosystem that government buyers (including via the Government e-Marketplace) can rely on to verify that a supplier's product carries a valid, current BIS licence, registration, or hallmark.

title: BIS Foundation Day and public outreach
content: BIS celebrates 6 January as its Foundation Day, commemorating the founding of its predecessor body, the Indian Standards Institution, on 6 January 1947. BIS marked its 78th Foundation Day on 6 January 2025, using the occasion for public outreach on the importance of standardization and quality in daily life.
source_name: Bureau of Indian Standards (secondary summary, Press Information Bureau)

title: BIS's role as India's WTO-TBT enquiry point
content: BIS functions as India's national enquiry point under the World Trade Organization's Agreement on Technical Barriers to Trade (WTO-TBT), receiving and responding to queries from other WTO member countries about Indian technical regulations, standards, and conformity-assessment procedures, and notifying India's own draft technical regulations for international comment.

title: BIS organizational structure - headquarters and regional offices
content: BIS is headquartered at Manak Bhawan, 9 Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg, New Delhi, and maintains a network of regional offices - Eastern Region (Kolkata), Southern Region (Chennai), Western Region (Mumbai), Northern Region (Chandigarh), and Central Region (Delhi) - along with around 20 branch offices located across the country, supporting BIS's certification, hallmarking, and standardization functions closer to industry and consumers.

title: Governing Council of BIS
content: As the National Standards Body, BIS is governed by a Governing Council of 25 members drawn from Central and State Governments, industry, scientific and research institutions, and consumer organizations. The minister in charge of the ministry with administrative control of BIS (currently the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution) is the ex-officio President of BIS.

title: BIS scientific and certification workforce
content: BIS employs more than 500 scientific officers who work as Certification Officers, Member Secretaries of technical committees, and Officers-in-Charge (OICs) of BIS laboratories, supporting its standardization, certification, hallmarking, and laboratory-testing functions nationwide.

title: National Quality Award administered by BIS
content: BIS administers a National Quality Award scheme recognizing organizations and individuals for outstanding contributions to quality, standardization, and conformity assessment in India, forming part of BIS's broader mandate to promote a culture of quality consciousness among manufacturers, institutions, and the public.

title: IS 302 (Part 1) - Household and Similar Electrical Appliances, Safety General Requirements
content: IS 302 (Part 1):2008 'Safety of household and similar electrical appliances: Part 1 General Requirements' (sixth revision) specifies general safety requirements and constructional details for household and similar electrical appliances, covering aspects such as marking and instructions, protection against live parts, motor starting tests, power/current input, heating, leakage current, electric strength, and ingress protection (IP) testing.
status: current, being phased out in favour of 2024 edition

status_parsed.raw: current, being phased out in favour of 2024 edition
status_parsed.notes: current, being phased out in favour of 2024 edition

title: IS 302 (Part 1):2024 - revision and concurrent running with the 2008 edition
content: IS 302 (Part 1):2008 has been revised and republished as IS 302 (Part 1):2024/IEC 60335-1:2020 'Household and Similar Electrical Appliances - Safety Part 1 General Requirements' (seventh revision), aligning the Indian Standard with IEC 60335-1:2020 and extending coverage to appliances with rated voltage up to 250V (single-phase) or 480V (other appliances), including DC and battery-operated appliances. Per a BIS circular, both the 2008 and 2024 editions were permitted to run concurrently for new licence applications until 23 February 2026, under the Safety of Household, Commercial and Similar Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2024.

title: IS 3196 (Part 1):2013 - Welded Low Carbon Steel Gas Cylinders for LPG
content: IS 3196 (Part 1):2013 'Welded Low Carbon Steel Gas Cylinders Exceeding 5 Litre Water Capacity for Low Pressure Liquefiable Gases - Part 1 Cylinders for LPG' covers requirements for welded low-carbon and high-tensile-strength steel gas cylinders for use with LPG, with nominal capacity above 5 litres and up to 250 litres, including terminology, material, design, welding, heat treatment, and performance tests such as capacity, hydrostatic, pneumatic leakage, fatigue, burst, and tensile tests. The standard does not apply to reconditioning of used LPG cylinders.

title: IS 3196 - other parts covering non-LPG and toxic/corrosive gas cylinders
content: The IS 3196 series extends beyond LPG cylinders: IS 3196 (Part 2) covers welded low-carbon steel gas cylinders for liquefiable gases other than LPG, and IS 3196 (Part 4) - 'Cylinders for Toxic and Corrosive Gases' (an amalgamation of the earlier IS 7680, IS 7681 and IS 7682) - covers welded low-carbon steel cylinders for toxic and corrosive gas service, specifying materials, welding quality, pressure relief devices, valve fittings, and testing protocols including hydraulic, burst-pressure, and leakage testing.

title: IS 6240 and IS 15914 - body material standards for LPG cylinders; IS 17613 for aluminium-alloy cylinders
content: The body material for welded LPG cylinders under IS 3196 (Part 1) must conform either to IS 6240 (low-carbon steel) or the high-tensile-strength material standard IS 15914. Separately, IS 17613:2021 prescribes requirements for welded aluminium-alloy gas cylinders for LPG use, of nominal capacity above 5 litres and up to 250 litres, as an alternative construction material to steel.

title: IS 8737 - Valve fittings for LPG cylinders
content: IS 8737 specifies requirements for valve fittings used with LPG cylinders of more than 5 litres water capacity, including Part 2 requirements for valve fittings for newly manufactured LPG cylinders, ensuring safe filling, dispensing, and pressure-relief performance of the cylinder valve assembly.

title: IS 2347:2017 - Domestic Pressure Cooker
content: IS 2347:2017 (reviewed 2022) covers domestic pressure cookers of nominal capacity up to 24 litres, including aluminium, stainless steel, hard-anodized, induction-compatible, composite-bottom, and 3-ply type cookers, specifying material, construction, safety devices, and performance test requirements to ensure the cooker safely withstands and releases internal pressure during cooking.

title: IS 4151:2015 - Protective Helmets for Two-Wheeler Riders
content: IS 4151:2015 'Protective Helmet for Two Wheeler Riders - Specification' (fourth revision) specifies materials, workmanship, finish, construction, and performance requirements for protective helmets, with or without a lower face cover, intended for everyday use by two-wheeler riders (not for high-speed competitive events). IS 4151 was first issued as an emergency Indian Standard in 1967; the 2015 edition updated impact-testing protocols and weight limits. The standard prescribes tests including rigidity, projection and surface friction, audibility, and quick-release-mechanism tests, alongside impact-absorption testing under varying temperature and humidity conditions.

title: IS 4151:2015 - headform sizes and provision for child pillion riders
content: IS 4151:2015 specifies headform sizes including two prominent sizes, 500 and 520, suited to children. Helmets with headform size below 500 conforming to the standard may be used as a 'crash helmet' for children, particularly those below age 4, while riding pillion on a two-wheeler, provided speed does not exceed 40 km/h - a provision introduced to address a Gazette Notification dated 15 February 2022 on child-pillion-rider helmet requirements.

title: IS 15298 (Part 1) - Personal Protective Equipment, Test Methods for Footwear
content: IS 15298 (Part 1):2024 (identical with ISO 20344:2021, second revision) specifies the test methods used to verify the requirements laid down in other parts of the IS 15298 series for personal protective equipment (PPE) footwear, covering safety, protective, and occupational footwear categories.

title: IS 15298 (Part 2) - Personal Protective Equipment, Safety Footwear
content: IS 15298 (Part 2):2016 'Personal Protective Equipment: Part 2 Safety Footwear' specifies basic and additional requirements for safety footwear, including a built-in, non-removable toecap tested to withstand compression loads of at least 15 kN and impact energy of at least 200 J. Footwear is classified as Code I (leather and other materials, excluding all-rubber/all-polymeric) or Code II (all-rubber or all-polymeric). A DPIIT Quality Control Order mandates that all safety footwear manufactured or imported in India comply with IS 15298 (Part 2):2016 and display the BIS Standard Mark.

title: IS 15298 (Part 3) - Personal Protective Equipment, Protective Footwear
content: IS 15298 (Part 3):2024 'Personal Protective Equipment: Part 3 Protective Footwear' (second revision) specifies requirements for protective footwear providing a lower level of impact/compression toe protection than safety footwear, for use where the risk of foot injury is present but less severe, aligned with ISO 20346.

title: IS 15298 (Part 4) - Personal Protective Equipment, Occupational Footwear
content: IS 15298 (Part 4):2017 'PPE - Occupational Footwear' specifies basic and additional requirements for occupational footwear - footwear with protective features intended to reduce the risk of injury to the wearer in general workplace settings, distinct from the higher-protection safety-footwear category under IS 15298 (Part 2).

title: IS 4985 - Unplasticized PVC (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supply
content: IS 4985 specifies requirements for unplasticized polyvinyl chloride (uPVC/PVC-U) pipes intended for carrying potable water under pressure, covering material composition (including a requirement for lead-free stabilizers in later editions), dimensions, physical and mechanical properties, and test methods for pipes across various pressure classes (nominally 2.5 to 15 kgf/cm2, corresponding to Classes 1 through 7).

title: IS 15778:2007 - Chlorinated PVC (CPVC) Pipes for Hot and Cold Water Distribution
content: IS 15778:2007 'Chlorinated Polyvinyl Chloride (CPVC) Pipes for Potable Hot and Cold Water Distribution Supplies - Specification' covers classification of pipes, chloride content of resin, compound properties, and verification of malfunction temperature (Tmal), among other requirements, for CPVC piping used in both hot- and cold-water plumbing distribution.

title: IS 10500:2012 - Drinking Water Specification
content: IS 10500:2012 (second revision) specifies the essential quality requirements for drinking water in India, defining an 'Acceptable Limit' and a relaxed 'Permissible Limit in the Absence of Alternate Source' for physical, chemical, bacteriological, and radiological parameters. The standard was first published in 1983. Key limits include pH 6.5-8.5 (no relaxation), Total Dissolved Solids 500/2000 mg/l, Total Hardness (as CaCO3) 200/600 mg/l, Chloride 250/1000 mg/l, Fluoride 1.0/1.5 mg/l, Nitrate 45 mg/l (no relaxation), Iron 0.3 mg/l, and minimum Residual Free Chlorine of 0.2 mg/l. It applies to piped public water supply and other drinking-water sources, but not to packaged drinking water, which is separately covered by IS 14543.

title: IS 10500:2012 - two-tier limit system explained
content: IS 10500:2012 uses a two-tier system unique among many national drinking-water standards: an 'Acceptable Limit' represents the preferred/desired level, above which water is not considered suitable even if not immediately harmful; a 'Permissible Limit in the Absence of Alternate Source' is a relaxed ceiling that may be tolerated only when no better water source is available. If a parameter exceeds the permissible limit, the source must be rejected as unfit for drinking.

title: IS 14543 - Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water)
content: IS 14543 is the Indian Standard specification governing packaged drinking water sold in sealed containers (other than natural mineral water, which is separately covered), setting quality parameters distinct from - though related to - the general drinking-water parameters in IS 10500:2012. BIS has produced educational 'BIS Talks' material specifically on packed drinking water to support consumer and manufacturer awareness of this standard.

title: IS 16046 (Part 1):2018 - Nickel-system secondary cells and batteries, safety requirements
content: IS 16046 (Part 1):2018/IEC 62133-1:2017 'Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Safety Requirements for Portable Sealed Secondary Cells and for Batteries Made from Them for Use in Portable Applications - Part 1 Nickel Systems' sets safety requirements for nickel-based rechargeable cells/batteries. It was published, together with IS 16046 (Part 2), to supersede the earlier combined IS 16046:2015/IEC 62133:2012, separating nickel and lithium chemistries into distinct parts and adding button-cell requirements; the last date for implementation of the revised standards was 14 March 2020, after which the earlier combined standard stood withdrawn.

title: IS 16046 (Part 2):2018 - Lithium-system secondary cells and batteries, safety requirements
content: IS 16046 (Part 2):2018/IEC 62133-2:2017 'Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Safety Requirements for Portable Sealed Secondary Cells and for Batteries Made from Them for Use in Portable Applications - Part 2 Lithium Systems' (second revision, reviewed 2024) is the mandatory safety standard for lithium-ion cells and batteries used in portable applications such as mobile phones and other consumer electronics, covering insulation/wiring, venting, temperature/voltage/current management, terminal contacts, assembly of cells into batteries, quality plan, and battery safety components, with type tests including crushing, forced discharge, over-charging, vibration, and temperature cycling.

title: IS 16270:2014 - Lead-acid Batteries specification
content: IS 16270:2014 sets rules for the safety, construction, and performance of lead-acid batteries, covering products such as automotive batteries, UPS batteries, solar-power-unit batteries, and small industrial batteries. It addresses capacity rating under specified discharge conditions and safety performance under short-circuit or high-temperature conditions, and is the primary standard underlying mandatory BIS Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) certification of lead-acid batteries.

title: IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 - Information Technology Equipment, Safety General Requirements
content: IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 'Information Technology Equipment - Safety: Part 1 General Requirements' (second revision) sets general safety requirements for IT equipment such as computers, servers, and related peripherals, covering protection from electric shock and energy hazards, power interfaces, and marking/instructions. It is one of the CRS-covered standards used to certify electronics and IT goods under BIS's Compulsory Registration Scheme, and is aligned with IEC 60950-1.

status_parsed.notes: current, second revision, mandatory under CRS

title: IS 616:2017 - Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus, Safety Requirements
content: IS 616:2017 sets safety requirements for audio, video, and similar electronic apparatus, aligned with IEC 60065, and is one of the standards covered under BIS's Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) for electronic and IT goods notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

title: IS 12269:2015 - Ordinary Portland Cement, 53 Grade
content: IS 12269:2015 specifies manufacturing, chemical, and physical requirements for 53 Grade Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC), used where high early and final strength is required, such as pre-stressed concrete, high-rise buildings, and infrastructure projects. Minimum compressive-strength requirements are 27 MPa at 3 days, 37 MPa at 7 days, and 53 MPa at 28 days (on standard mortar cubes tested per IS 4031), with an initial setting time of at least 30 minutes and a final setting time not exceeding 600 minutes.

title: IS 1489 (Part 1):2015 - Portland Pozzolana Cement, fly-ash based
content: IS 1489 (Part 1):2015 'Portland Pozzolana Cement - Specification: Part 1 Fly Ash Based' (fourth revision) specifies the manufacturing and quality requirements for Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) made using fly ash as the pozzolanic material, an alternative to Ordinary Portland Cement offering different heat-of-hydration and durability characteristics, particularly relevant for mass-concrete and durability-sensitive applications.

title: IS 4031 (Parts 1 to 15) - Methods of Physical Tests for Hydraulic Cement
content: IS 4031 (Parts 1 to 15) prescribes the standard methods of physical testing for hydraulic cement in India, including tests for fineness, setting time, soundness, and compressive strength (Part 6, on standard sand per IS 650), underpinning grade classifications used across the cement family of standards such as IS 269 (OPC), IS 1489 (PPC), IS 455 (PSC), and IS 12269 (OPC 53 Grade).

title: IS 3025 - Methods of Sampling and Test (Physical and Chemical) for Water and Wastewater
content: IS 3025 (issued in multiple parts) prescribes the methods of sampling and physical/chemical testing for water and wastewater in India, and is the referenced test-method standard used alongside IS 10500:2012 to determine whether a water sample's parameters (turbidity, odour, taste, dissolved solids, and various chemical constituents) meet the acceptable or permissible limits for drinking water.

title: IS 1943:1995 - A-twill Jute Bags
content: IS 1943:1995 is the Indian Standard specification for A-twill jute bags, one of two jute-bag standards (alongside IS 2566:1993) brought under compulsory BIS certification through the Jute Bags (Quality Control) Order, 2022 issued by the Ministry of Textiles, effective 6 June 2022, reflecting the government's continued policy support for jute packaging in select sectors.

title: IS 2566:1993 - B-twill Jute Bags for Packing Foodgrains
content: IS 2566:1993 is the Indian Standard specification for B-twill jute bags used for packing foodgrains, brought under compulsory BIS certification through the Jute Bags (Quality Control) Order, 2022 issued by the Ministry of Textiles, effective 6 June 2022.

title: IS 9755:2021 - HDPE/PP Woven Sacks for Packaging Fertilizers
content: IS 9755:2021 'Textiles - High Density Polyethylene (HDPE)/Polypropylene (PP) Woven Sacks for Packaging Fertilizers - Specification' is the Indian Standard underlying the Textiles - HDPE/PP Woven Sacks for Packaging Fertilizers (Quality Control) Order, 2023, mandating that woven sacks used to package fertilizer conform to this specification and bear the BIS Standard Mark.

title: IS 17265:2022 - 100% Polyester Spun, Grey and White Yarn
content: IS 17265:2022 is the Indian Standard for 100% Polyester Spun Grey and White Yarn (PSY), one of several polyester-product standards notified for compulsory BIS certification by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals), effective 3 April 2023, subsequently rescinded along with several related polyester QCOs by government orders dated 12 November 2025.

title: IS 17261/17262/17263/17264:2022 - Polyester yarn and fibre family of standards
content: Alongside IS 17265:2022, BIS's polyester-product standards include IS 17261:2022 (Polyester Continuous Filament Fully Drawn Yarn, FDY), IS 17262:2022 (Polyester Partially Oriented Yarn, POY), IS 17263:2022 (Polyester Staple Fibres, PSF), and IS 17264:2022 (Polyester Industrial Yarn, IDY). These were notified for compulsory certification by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers effective 3 April 2023, and were subsequently rescinded, along with related chemical/polymer QCOs, through Government orders dated 12 November 2025.

title: IS 1638:1969 - Sizes and Fitting of Footwear
content: IS 1638:1969 'Specification for Sizes and Fitting of Footwear' (first revision) is a foundational Indian Standard defining the sizing and fitting system used across the Indian footwear industry, complementing product-specific standards such as the IS 15298 personal-protective-equipment footwear series.

title: IS 875 (Parts 1 to 5) - Code of Practice for Design Loads (Other Than Earthquake)
content: IS 875 (Parts 1 to 5) is the Indian Standard code of practice for design loads on buildings and structures, other than earthquake loads - covering dead loads, imposed (live) loads, wind loads, snow loads, and special loads/load combinations. It is used together with the explanatory handbook SP 64 and is a core reference alongside IS 456:2000 for structural design in India.

title: IS 1893 - Criteria for Earthquake Resistant Design of Structures
content: IS 1893 is BIS's Indian Standard code covering criteria for earthquake-resistant design of structures in India, defining seismic zones, design horizontal seismic coefficients, and design provisions used alongside IS 456:2000 and IS 13920:2016 for reinforced-concrete structures located in earthquake-prone regions.

title: IS 13920:2016 - Ductile Detailing of Reinforced Concrete Structures Subjected to Seismic Forces
content: IS 13920:2016 'Ductile Detailing of Reinforced Concrete Structures Subjected to Seismic Forces - Code of Practice' supplements IS 456:2000 by prescribing detailing requirements (reinforcement anchorage, confinement, and joint detailing) needed to ensure ductile behaviour of reinforced-concrete beams, columns, and joints during earthquakes, and is a mandatory reference for RCC design in India's seismic zones.

title: Standard designation and numbering convention (IS number : year)
content: An Indian Standard is conventionally cited as 'IS' followed by a serial number and, after a colon, the year of the current edition (e.g., IS 456:2000), with multi-part standards adding a '(Part n)' or '(Part n/Sec m)' designation (e.g., IS 516 (Part 1/Sec 1):2021). Where a standard is technically identical to an international standard, BIS may cite both numbers together, e.g., IS 302 (Part 1):2024/IEC 60335-1:2020.

title: Meaning of 'Reviewed' status against an Indian Standard
content: BIS periodically reviews published Indian Standards to determine whether they should be reaffirmed as-is, revised, or withdrawn. A standard catalogue entry marked 'Reviewed in [year]' (e.g., 'IS 2347:2017 Reviewed In: 2022') indicates BIS's technical committee examined the standard in that year and determined it did not yet require revision, distinguishing this from a full revision, which produces a new dated edition of the standard.

title: Reaffirmation, revision, and amendment - distinct forms of updating a standard
content: BIS distinguishes three ways a standard can be updated: 'reaffirmation', where a standard is examined and kept unchanged for continued validity (e.g., IS 456:2000 was reaffirmed after periodic review); 'revision', where a standard is substantively rewritten and issued as a new numbered edition/version (e.g., the fourth revision of IS 456, or the fourth revision of IS 1786:2008); and 'amendment', where a discrete, numbered correction or addition (Amendment 1, Amendment 2, etc.) is issued against an existing edition without a full revision.

title: Withdrawal of an Indian Standard
content: An Indian Standard may be formally withdrawn by BIS when it is superseded by a revised or replacement standard, or is no longer considered relevant to current industry practice - for example, the combined IS 16046:2015/IEC 62133:2012 battery-safety standard stood withdrawn once its replacement parts, IS 16046 (Part 1):2018 and IS 16046 (Part 2):2018, took mandatory effect on 14 March 2020.

title: Adoption of ISO/IEC standards as identical Indian Standards
content: BIS frequently adopts international ISO or IEC standards as Indian Standards under 'dual numbering', citing both designations together (for example, IS 16046 (Part 2):2018/IEC 62133-2:2017, or IS 302 (Part 1):2024/IEC 60335-1:2020). Where a standard is adopted this way, BIS's catalogue records a 'Degree of Equivalence' - such as 'Identical under dual numbering' - describing how closely the Indian Standard's technical content matches the source international standard.

title: IS/ISO dual-numbered management-system standards
content: BIS's management-systems standards are commonly dual-numbered with their ISO counterparts to signal identical technical adoption, for example IS/ISO 9001 (Quality Management Systems), IS/ISO 14001 (Environmental Management Systems), IS/ISO 45001 (Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems), IS/ISO 50001 (Energy Management Systems), and IS/ISO 37001 (Anti-Bribery Management Systems) - the same convention used for Systems Certification under BIS's Management Systems Certification Scheme.

title: 'Superseding IS' and 'Number of Revisions' fields in the BIS standards catalogue
content: BIS's online 'Know Your Standards' catalogue records, for each Indian Standard, whether it supersedes an earlier standard number (field: 'Superseding IS') and how many times it has been revised (field: 'Number of Revisions'). A standard newly introduced without replacing an earlier one is marked 'New Standard' with 'Superseding IS: None' - for example, IS 16046 (Part 2):2018 is recorded as a 'New Standard' in this sense, since it replaced only a part of the combined IS 16046:2015.

title: National Building Code of India (SP 7)
content: The National Building Code of India is published by BIS as Special Publication SP 7 (e.g., 'SP 7: Group 1: 2005'), providing comprehensive guidelines for building design, construction, and safety across India, and cross-referencing numerous individual Indian Standards including those on cement, concrete, and structural design such as IS 456:2000.

title: BIS Special Publications (SP series) - handbooks and design aids
content: Beyond regular Indian Standards, BIS publishes a series of 'Special Publications' (SP), which include explanatory handbooks and design aids that support engineers in applying the corresponding Indian Standard - for example, SP 16-1980 'Design Aids for Reinforced Concrete to IS 456-1978' (still used by structural engineers as a rapid-design reference despite being based on the 1978 edition of IS 456), SP 34 (Handbook on Concrete Reinforcement and Detailing), and SP 64 (Explanatory Handbook on IS 875, design loads).

title: Sectional/Technical Committee example - Cement and Concrete Sectional Committee (CED 02)
content: Indian Standards in the cement and concrete family - such as IS 269 (OPC), IS 455 (PSC), IS 456 (plain and reinforced concrete), IS 1489 (PPC), and IS 12269 (OPC 53 Grade) - are formulated and maintained under the Cement and Concrete Sectional Committee, designated 'CED 02', within BIS's Civil Engineering Division. Committee codes like 'CED 02' or 'CHD 19' (Leather and Leather Products, covering footwear standards such as IS 15298) appear against each Indian Standard in BIS's online catalogue to identify the responsible technical committee.

title: IS 1200 - Method of Measurement of Building and Civil Engineering Works
content: IS 1200 (issued in multiple parts) prescribes standard methods of measurement for building and civil engineering works in India, providing a uniform basis for quantity estimation, billing, and contract administration across construction trades such as earthwork, concrete, masonry, and finishing works.

title: IS 2911 - Design and Construction of Pile Foundations, Code of Practice
content: IS 2911 is the Indian Standard code of practice for the design and construction of pile foundations, referenced alongside IS 1892 (Subsurface Investigation for Foundations) and IS 456:2000 in foundation-engineering practice for buildings and structures in India.

title: IS 4926 - Ready-Mixed Concrete, Code of Practice
content: IS 4926 'Ready-Mixed Concrete - Code of Practice' specifies requirements for the production, quality control, and delivery of ready-mixed concrete (RMC) supplied from a batching plant to a construction site, and is the standard underlying BIS's Ready Mixed Concrete Certification Scheme, which combines conformity to IS 4926 with an ISO 9001-based process certification.

title: IS 1077 and IS 3495 - Bricks for Masonry Work and Methods of Testing Bricks
content: IS 1077 specifies requirements for common burnt-clay building bricks used in masonry work, while IS 3495 prescribes the methods of testing bricks (such as compressive strength, water absorption, and efflorescence testing); IS 5454 separately covers methods of sampling bricks for such tests. These standards are foundational references for masonry construction quality control in India.

title: 'Grouping guidelines' concept in BIS Product Manuals
content: BIS Product Manuals for certified products commonly include 'Grouping Guidelines' (typically set out in an Annex), which define how different sizes, grades, or varieties of a product manufactured by the same licensee can be grouped for the purpose of sampling and testing under the Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), reducing the testing burden for closely related product variants without compromising conformity assurance.

title: IS 4250 - Household Mixer Grinders
content: IS 4250 is the Indian Standard governing household mixer grinders, one of the household electrical appliance product standards BIS has profiled in its 'BIS Talks' educational video series to explain manufacturing and testing requirements to consumers and industry, alongside general safety requirements under IS 302 (Part 1).

title: IS 7098 (Part 1 and Part 2) - PVC Insulated (Heavy Duty) Electric Cables
content: IS 7098 (Parts 1 and 2) specifies requirements for PVC-insulated (heavy duty) electric cables for working voltages up to and including 1100V, a widely used cable standard in India's electrical infrastructure, and is one of the product standards BIS has documented through its 'BIS Talks' outreach video series.

title: IS 9873 - family of parts covering non-electric toy safety
content: Beyond IS 9873 (Part 1):2019 (general safety requirements for non-electric toys), the IS 9873 series includes further parts applied as secondary standards depending on a toy's materials and features - referenced parts include Part 2 (flammability), Part 3 (migration of certain elements), Part 4 (swings, slides and similar activity toys), Part 7 (finger paints), and Part 9 (certain phthalate esters in toys and children's products), all of which may apply alongside Part 1 under India's Toys (Quality Control) Order, 2020.

title: IS 14899 and IS 15100 - LPG containers and valve assemblies for automotive use
content: IS 14899 specifies requirements for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) containers for automotive use (autogas cylinders), while IS 15100 specifies requirements for the multifunction valve assembly used with permanently fixed LPG containers in automotive applications - both forming part of BIS's family of standards for gas-cylinder and valve products, alongside the IS 3196 series for stationary/domestic LPG cylinders.

title: IS 7285 (Part 1 and Part 2) - Refillable Seamless Steel Gas Cylinders
content: IS 7285 (Part 1) covers refillable seamless steel gas cylinders made from normalized steel, while IS 7285 (Part 2) covers refillable seamless steel gas cylinders made from quenched-and-tempered steel with tensile strength less than 1100 MPa (112 kgf/mm2) - standards used for high-pressure gas cylinders distinct from the welded low-carbon-steel cylinders covered by IS 3196.

title: IS 12269 - editions and legacy status
content: IS 12269 (Ordinary Portland Cement, 53 Grade) has been published in successive editions - 1987, 2013, and 2015 - with the 2015 edition being the current specification for new work; the earlier 1987 and 2013 editions remain relevant only for reference against legacy structures or historical project documentation, illustrating how BIS's edition history for a widely used standard can span decades of incremental technical updates.

title: IS 1660 and IS 14756 - Aluminium and Stainless Steel Cookware
content: IS 1660:2009 (reviewed 2021) specifies quality-of-material and thickness requirements for aluminium cookware such as wrought aluminium utensils, thick-bottomed utensils, compartmental trays, and lunch boxes. IS 14756:2022 covers stainless steel cookware, including cooking, serving, table, and storage utensils, complementing the domestic pressure cooker standard IS 2347:2017 within BIS's kitchenware product family.

title: IS 16218 and IS 16286 - Table and Serving Cutlery (Forks and Spoons)
content: IS 16218:2014 (reviewed 2020) specifies requirements for various types of forks, including table/serving, dessert, fish, and pastry forks. IS 16286:2014 (reviewed 2020) covers various types of spoons, including large serving spoons, table/serving spoons, dessert spoons, tea spoons, baby spoons, coffee spoons, soup spoons, and mustard/salt spoons - part of BIS's broader domestic-tableware product category alongside cookware standards.

title: IS 17011:2018 - Chemical Requirements for Footwear and Footwear Materials
content: IS 17011:2018 (reviewed 2023) specifies chemical requirements applicable to footwear and footwear materials, complementing the mechanical/performance requirements of the IS 15298 personal-protective-equipment footwear series and general footwear standards such as IS 1638 (sizing) and IS 2050 (glossary of footwear terms).

title: BIS Division Councils spanning textile, leather and chemical sectors
content: Among BIS's 16 Division Councils, standards relevant to consumer and industrial products are formulated by sector-specific technical departments - for example, the Textile Division (TXD, covering standards like IS 9755 for HDPE/PP woven sacks and IS 14358 for nylon shoe laces), the Chemical Division (CHD, covering leather and footwear standards such as IS 15298 and IS 17011), and the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division (PCD, covering rubber-testing standards such as IS 3400) - illustrating the breadth of sectors BIS standardizes beyond civil and mechanical engineering.

title: IS 3400 (Part 2) - Methods of Test for Vulcanized Rubber, Hardness
content: IS 3400 (Part 2):2023 (identical with ISO 48-2:2018, fourth revision) specifies the method of test for determining the hardness of vulcanized or thermoplastic rubber, for hardness values between 10 and 100 IRHD (International Rubber Hardness Degrees), a widely used test-method standard for rubber components including footwear soles and gaskets.

title: IS 9755:2021 supersedes an earlier edition of the fertilizer woven-sack standard
content: The catalogue entry for IS 9755:2021 identifies it as the current specification for HDPE/PP woven sacks used to package fertilizers, and its implementation date under the corresponding Quality Control Order was later postponed by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (via a notification dated 4 June 2024) to 6 September 2024, giving affected manufacturers additional time to comply.

title: IS 16481:2022 - Synthetic Micro-Fibres for Use in Cement-Based Matrix
content: IS 16481:2022 'Synthetic Micro-Fibres for Use in Cement Based Matrix' is one of the polyester/synthetic-fibre-family standards notified for compulsory BIS certification by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals) effective 3 April 2023, covering fibres used as crack-control reinforcement additives in cement/concrete products.

title: Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products standard family under QCO
content: BIS's Aluminium and Aluminium Alloy Products (Quality Control) Order, 2023 (effective 27 March 2024) brought aluminium and aluminium-alloy product standards under compulsory certification, part of the government's broader effort in 2023 to extend Quality Control Orders across metals, chemicals, and engineering product categories with staggered implementation dates and extended compliance windows for small and micro enterprises.

title: Diesel Engines - NOx Reduction Agent AUS 32 (Quality Control) Order, 2023
content: The Diesel Engines - NOx Reduction Agent AUS 32 (Quality Control) Order, 2023 brought the Indian Standard governing AUS 32 (Aqueous Urea Solution, used as a diesel-exhaust NOx-reduction agent, commonly known as Diesel Exhaust Fluid) under compulsory BIS certification, part of a set of engineering-sector QCOs notified in 2023.

title: Anhydrous Ammonia (Quality Control) Order, 2023
content: The Anhydrous Ammonia (Quality Control) Order, 2023 brought the Indian Standard governing anhydrous ammonia - an important industrial chemical used in fertilizer production and refrigeration - under compulsory BIS certification, issued by the relevant chemical-sector ministry as part of the broader 2023 wave of QCOs covering industrial chemicals.

title: IS 2050 - Glossary of Terms Relating to Footwear
content: IS 2050:1991 (first revision) is BIS's glossary of terms relating to footwear, providing standardized terminology used across the footwear-standards family, including IS 1638 (sizes and fitting), IS 15298 (PPE footwear), and IS 17011 (chemical requirements).

title: IS 6519:1971 - Code of Practice for Selection, Care and Repair of Safety Footwear
content: IS 6519:1971 provides a code of practice for the selection, care, and repair of safety footwear, intended to guide employers and workers on proper use and maintenance of safety footwear conforming to standards such as IS 15298 (Part 2), extending BIS's footwear-safety framework beyond manufacturing specification into in-service guidance.

title: IS 9543:2015 - Spun Polyester Sewing Threads
content: IS 9543:2015 (first revision, reviewed 2019) specifies requirements for spun polyester sewing threads, a textile-product standard within BIS's TXD (Textile Division) technical department, relevant to garment and footwear manufacturing (including stitching components used alongside footwear standards such as IS 15298).

title: IS 14358 - Nylon Laces for Shoes and Boots
content: IS 14358 'Textiles - Nylon Laces for Shoes and Boots - Specification' governs nylon lace components used in footwear manufacturing; the standard's catalogue entry has been updated over time (from a 1996 edition, reviewed 2019, to a 2024 edition), reflecting BIS's periodic-review cycle applied even to component-level textile standards feeding into larger product categories like footwear.

title: IS 12240 (Part 4):1988 - Test Methods for PVC used in Boots (Volatility)
content: IS 12240 (Part 4):1988 (reviewed 2023) specifies the method of test for determining volatility of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) material used in the manufacture of boots, one of several material-level PVC test-method standards feeding into finished-product footwear standards such as the IS 15298 series.

title: Quality Control Order (QCO) - legal mechanism and issuing authority
content: A Quality Control Order (QCO) is issued by the relevant Central Government line ministry or regulator (after consultation with BIS) under the BIS Act, 2016, mandating that specified goods or articles conform to a designated Indian Standard and bear the BIS Standard Mark under a valid licence, in the public interest, for consumer protection, or to curb substandard goods. Products under QCOs are governed by the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018, and violation of a QCO is punishable under the BIS Act with imprisonment, fine, or both. QCOs are also intended to align with India's obligations under the WTO Agreement on Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT).

title: Jute Bags (Quality Control) Order, 2022 - Ministry of Textiles
content: The Jute Bags (Quality Control) Order, 2022, issued by the Ministry of Textiles with effect from 6 June 2022, brought two products under compulsory BIS certification: A-twill jute bags (IS 1943:1995) and B-twill jute bags for packing foodgrains (IS 2566:1993). This QCO illustrates that Quality Control Orders are issued by the specific line ministry responsible for a product sector, not by BIS itself, though BIS administers the resulting licensing and certification.

title: Polyester yarn and fibre QCOs - Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers
content: The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals) issued Quality Control Orders effective 3 April 2023 bringing several polyester yarn/fibre products under compulsory BIS certification: 100% Polyester Spun Grey and White Yarn (IS 17265:2022), Polyester Continuous Filament Fully Drawn Yarn (IS 17261:2022), Polyester Industrial Yarn (IS 17264:2022), Polyester Partially Oriented Yarn (IS 17262:2022), Polyester Staple Fibres (IS 17263:2022), and Synthetic Micro-Fibres for use in Cement-Based Matrix (IS 16481:2022). Several of these QCOs were subsequently rescinded by Government orders dated 12 November 2025.

title: HDPE/PP Woven Sack QCOs for cement, fertilizer, and polymer packaging
content: The Ministry of Textiles issued a set of Quality Control Orders in 2023 covering woven-sack packaging materials: HDPE/PP Woven Sacks for Packaging of 50 kg Cement; PP Woven, Laminated, Block-Bottom Valve Sacks for Packaging of 50 kg Cement; HDPE/PP Woven Sacks for Packaging Fertilizers (IS 9755:2021); HDPE/PP Woven Sacks for Packaging of 25 kg Polymer Materials; and HDPE/PP Laminated Woven Sacks for Mail Sorting, Storage, Transport and Distribution. Implementation dates for several of these were subsequently postponed by amendment orders to give industry more compliance time.

title: Helmet for Riders of Two-Wheeler Motor Vehicles (Quality Control) Order, 2020
content: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways notified the Helmet for Riders of Two-Wheeler Motor Vehicles (Quality Control) Order, 2020 (reference S.O. No. 4252(E), dated 26 November 2020), making BIS certification against IS 4151:2015 mandatory for protective helmets used by two-wheeler riders in India, reinforcing consumer confidence in helmet safety and quality.

title: Safety Footwear Quality Control Order - DPIIT
content: The Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) issued a Quality Control Order mandating that all safety footwear manufactured or imported in India comply with IS 15298 (Part 2):2016 and display the BIS Standard Mark, covering both domestically produced and imported safety footwear under the Product Certification (ISI Mark) Scheme.

title: BIS certification route for lithium-ion batteries under CRS
content: Lithium-ion cells and batteries are certified under BIS's Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS), based on self-declaration of conformity to IS 16046 (Part 2):2018/IEC 62133-2:2017, following product testing at a BIS-recognized laboratory. Each cell/battery model covered under CRS must be BIS-registered and bear the Standard Mark with a unique registration number; both domestic manufacturers and importers/brand owners selling products containing lithium cells (e.g., e-bikes, energy storage systems, power banks) must register, and foreign manufacturers must appoint an Authorized Indian Representative (AIR).

title: BIS verification guidelines for rated capacity of lithium cells and batteries (2026)
content: Following an order dated 3 February 2026 from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), BIS updated its Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) guidelines for lithium-ion cells and batteries to require that rated capacity be measured and reported in compliance with the relevant IS 16047 clause on standardized capacity testing, addressing concerns that some CRS-registered products carried exaggerated capacity claims inconsistent with independent laboratory results. Manufacturers were required to update their online CRS profiles and application records with verified capacity data.

title: BIS certification route for lead-acid batteries under CRS
content: Lead-acid batteries used in automobiles, UPS systems, solar power units, and small industrial tools are subject to mandatory BIS CRS certification against IS 16270:2014, which governs safety, construction, and performance requirements including capacity rating, short-circuit/high-temperature safety, shelf-life, and long-term storage performance. Certification follows the standard CRS pathway: application filing with technical documents, testing at a BIS-recognized laboratory, and grant of registration with a unique R-number.

title: Electric Equipment Quality Control Order (EEQCO), 2020 - Ministry of Heavy Industries
content: The Electric Equipment Quality Control Order, 2020 (EEQCO), issued by the Ministry of Heavy Industries, has been implemented in phases; its first phase came into effect on 10 November 2024. Following this, the Ministry issued guidance on identifying products covered under the phased implementation, which was circulated by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) to Customs field officers to support enforcement at ports of entry.

title: Steel and Steel Products Quality Control Order - Ministry of Steel
content: The Ministry of Steel administers the Steel and Steel Products Quality Control Order, which mandates that a wide range of steel products (including hot-rolled structural steel under IS 2062:2011 and reinforcement bars/wires under IS 1786:2008) be certified against the relevant Indian Standard before sale in India. The order has been periodically amended - for example, an amendment notified around 20 November 2025 - reflecting the government's continued expansion and fine-tuning of steel-sector quality control.

title: Safety of Household, Commercial and Similar Electrical Appliances (Quality Control) Order, 2024
content: This QCO requires manufacturers of electrical appliances within its scope (single-phase up to 250V AC or three-phase up to 415V AC, not already covered by another QCO) to obtain a BIS certification licence as per IS 302 (Part 1) under Scheme-I of the BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018. Appliances already covered by another specific QCO are excluded from this order's scope, with BIS publishing a reference annexure listing such excluded appliances to avoid dual-certification confusion.

title: Concurrent running provision when a certification standard is revised
content: When a mandatory product standard is revised (as with IS 302 (Part 1), revised from the 2008 to the 2024/IEC 60335-1:2020 edition), BIS may permit a 'concurrent running' period during which manufacturers can apply for a licence under either the old or new edition of the standard. For the IS 302 (Part 1) transition, both editions were permitted for new applications until 23 February 2026, giving industry a defined transition window before the older edition's licensing route closed.

title: MSME and Small/Micro Enterprise grace periods under QCOs
content: Quality Control Orders typically provide additional compliance time for smaller businesses: an additional 3 months for Small Enterprises and an additional 6 months for Micro Enterprises, beyond the standard implementation date applicable to larger manufacturers, reflecting the government's policy of easing the compliance burden on MSMEs while still bringing products under mandatory certification.

title: QCO exemption for Advance Authorization holders, EOUs and SEZs
content: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Ministry of Commerce & Industry, has issued Public Notices exempting imports made by Advance Authorization holders, Export Oriented Units (EOUs), and Special Economic Zone (SEZ) units - where the imported goods are to be consumed/utilized in export production - from compliance with QCOs notified by certain ministries/departments, including the Ministry of Heavy Industries, recognizing that such imports are not destined for the domestic consumer market.

title: Rescission (withdrawal) of Quality Control Orders
content: A QCO can be rescinded (withdrawn) by the issuing ministry in the public interest, after consultation with BIS, under Section 16 of the BIS Act, 2016 - removing the corresponding product from mandatory BIS certification. Notable examples include the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers rescinding 14 chemical/polymer QCOs (including products like Terephthalic Acid, Ethylene Glycol, and several polyester products) through orders dated 12 November 2025, and the Ministry of Textiles withdrawing the Viscose Staple Fibres QCO on 18 November 2025.

title: International concerns raised at the WTO over BIS certification timelines
content: At a meeting of the WTO Goods Council, Thailand and Indonesia raised concerns regarding perceived non-transparency and delays in the grant of certifications by BIS, contending such delays act as import restrictions and trade barriers; India responded that it remained committed to facilitating international trade while ensuring product quality, and would work to resolve the concerns through bilateral discussions. Separately, Japan's Embassy in India raised concerns with the Ministry of Steel and Ministry of Commerce and Industry over Japanese steel consignments being held at Indian ports pending BIS-related clearance issues.

title: 'All India First Licence' - significance for a newly notified Indian Standard
content: When BIS grants the first-ever product certification licence for a given Indian Standard under Scheme-I (an 'All India First Licence'), the issuance is treated as a milestone that paves the way for subsequent applicants, since it typically confirms the finalized Product Manual, Scheme of Inspection and Testing (SIT), and marking-fee structure for that standard have been successfully applied in practice.

title: Guideline for grant of licence under Scheme-I
content: BIS's Product Certification Process (Scheme-I) is governed by a set of published guidelines, one of which is the 'Guideline for Grant of Licence', setting out the procedural steps BIS follows - factory assessment, sample testing, and documentation review - before granting a manufacturer a certification licence to use the Standard Mark on a specific product.

title: Guideline for renewal of licence
content: BIS's 'Guideline for Renewal of Licence' sets out the process by which an existing product-certification licensee applies to extend the validity of its BIS licence before expiry, including the documents and fees required and the timeline within which a renewal application should be submitted to avoid a lapse in certification.

title: Guideline for suspension and revocation of suspension of licence
content: BIS's 'Guideline for Suspension and Revocation of Suspension of Licence' governs the circumstances and process under which a licensee's certification may be temporarily suspended (for example, following a failed conformity test or a compliance lapse) and the process by which such a suspension may later be revoked once the licensee demonstrates corrective action.

title: Guideline for change in scope of licence
content: BIS's 'Guideline for Change in Scope of Licence' governs how an existing licensee can apply to add, modify, or remove varieties, grades, or sizes of a product covered under its existing BIS certification licence, without needing to apply for an entirely new licence.

title: Guideline for retesting of samples
content: BIS's 'Guideline for Retesting of Samples' sets out the procedure a licensee may follow to request retesting of a product sample that has failed conformity testing, including conditions under which retesting is permitted and how the outcome affects the licensee's certification status.

title: Guideline for operation of licence
content: BIS's 'Guideline for Operation of Licence' covers the ongoing obligations of a licensee during the currency of its certification - including maintaining quality control records, using the Standard Mark correctly, cooperating with surveillance visits, and submitting periodic returns - distinct from the one-time processes of grant, renewal, or scope change.

title: Marking fee - definition and periodicity
content: The 'marking fee' under BIS product certification is the recurring fee a licensee pays for the right to use the BIS Standard Mark on certified products, typically assessed and payable on a quarterly basis (with a minimum quarterly amount), separate from the one-time application fee, per-visit inspection fee, and periodic renewal application fee.

title: Surveillance and market sampling under BIS product certification
content: BIS carries out surveillance of licensed manufacturers - through periodic factory visits and market sample collection - to verify continued conformity of certified products to the relevant Indian Standard after a licence has been granted, complementing the initial factory-assessment and testing steps carried out before certification. Non-conforming surveillance samples can trigger the suspension or cancellation processes set out in BIS's licensing guidelines.

title: BIS licence number format (CM/L number)
content: A BIS product-certification licence is commonly referenced by a licence number in the format 'CM/L-[number]' (Certification Marks Licence number), which appears on the licensee's certificate and is used to verify the licence's details (product, varieties, validity) via BIS's online licence-search facilities such as manakonline.in or the BIS Care app.

title: ISI mark - visual identity of the BIS Standard Mark for product certification
content: The ISI Mark is BIS's Standard Mark used under the Product Certification Scheme (Scheme-I), a licensed logo that a certified manufacturer is permitted to display on products conforming to the relevant Indian Standard. The mark is recognized nationally as a visible assurance of BIS-certified quality, distinct from the Hallmark (used for gold/silver jewellery) and the CRS registration mark (used for electronics/IT goods), even though all three are variants of BIS's overall 'Standard Mark' concept under the BIS Act, 2016.

title: Certificate of Conformity (CoC) as an alternative to a BIS licence
content: Under certain QCOs, a manufacturer may be permitted to obtain either a full BIS licence or a Certificate of Conformity (CoC) as an alternative route to demonstrate conformity with the mandatory Indian Standard - after the effective date of a QCO, no person may manufacture, import, distribute, sell, hire, lease, store, or exhibit for sale a covered product without a valid Licence or Certificate of Conformity from BIS bearing the Standard Mark.

title: ECO Mark Scheme - eligibility criteria
content: BIS's ECO Mark Scheme certifies consumer products that meet specified environment-friendly criteria - covering considerations such as reduced environmental impact of raw materials, manufacturing process, use, and disposal - allowing eligible products to carry the ECO Mark alongside (or as part of) their BIS certification, distinct from the general ISI product-quality certification.

title: ECO Mark logo
content: The BIS ECO Mark uses a distinctive logo depicting an earthen pot ('matka'), symbolizing environmentally friendly products, and is displayed on eligible product packaging alongside the manufacturer's other BIS certification marks where applicable, forming part of India's eco-labelling framework administered by BIS under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change's broader eco-labelling criteria.

title: Medical device certification pathway - IS/ISO 13485 and product-specific standards
content: Medical devices in India may require both a Quality Management System certification against IS/ISO 13485 (Medical Devices - Quality Management System) under BIS's Systems Certification scheme and, where applicable, product-specific certification against the relevant medical-device Indian Standard, reflecting the dual system-plus-product approach BIS applies in some regulated sectors alongside the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation's (CDSCO) separate regulatory regime for medical devices.

title: CRS unique registration ('R') number
content: Upon successful registration under the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS), BIS issues a unique registration number (commonly referred to as an 'R-number') that must be marked on the CRS-covered electronic/IT product alongside the Standard Mark, enabling market surveillance authorities and consumers to trace the product back to its registered manufacturer and applicable Indian Standard via the crsbis.in portal or the BIS Care app.

title: CRS self-declaration vs Scheme-I factory-inspection model
content: CRS registration (Scheme-II) differs procedurally from Scheme-I product certification: CRS is based primarily on a manufacturer's self-declaration of conformity, supported by test reports from a BIS-recognized laboratory, without a mandatory factory-inspection visit at the point of initial registration, whereas Scheme-I product certification requires BIS to conduct a factory assessment of manufacturing infrastructure, process controls, and quality-control/testing capability before granting a licence.

title: FMCS - product categories excluded (Electronics and IT Goods)
content: The Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) explicitly excludes Electronics and IT Goods notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) from its scope; such goods, whether from domestic or foreign manufacturers, are instead certified through the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) operated via crsbis.in, keeping electronics/IT certification administratively distinct from BIS's general FMCS route for other product categories.

title: FMCS - Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) responsibilities
content: A foreign manufacturer's Authorized Indian Representative (AIR) under FMCS acts as the local point of contact responsible for preparing and submitting the BIS certification application, liaising with BIS during factory assessment and testing, and managing ongoing compliance and communication with BIS on the foreign manufacturer's behalf, as the AIR must be resident in India per BIS's FMCS requirements.

title: Systems Certification - Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP), IS 15000
content: BIS offers certification against IS 15000, India's Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) standard, used by food-industry organizations to systematically identify and control food-safety hazards throughout production, complementing BIS's broader Food Safety Management System certification (IS/ISO 22000).

title: Systems Certification - Adventure Tourism Safety Management System, IS/ISO 21101
content: BIS offers certification against IS/ISO 21101:2014, the Adventure Tourism Safety Management System standard, applicable to organizations offering adventure-tourism activities in India, reflecting BIS's extension of management-systems certification beyond manufacturing into services sectors such as tourism.

title: Systems Certification - Road Traffic Safety Management System, IS/ISO 39001
content: BIS offers certification against IS/ISO 39001, the Road Traffic Safety Management System standard, applicable to organizations (such as fleet operators or transport agencies) seeking to systematically manage and reduce road-traffic-related risk within their operations, part of BIS's growing portfolio of sector-specific management-system certifications.

title: Systems Certification - Educational Organizations Management System, IS/ISO 21001
content: BIS offers certification against IS/ISO 21001, the Educational Organizations Management System standard (based on the structure of IS/ISO 9001), applicable to schools, colleges, and other education-sector organizations seeking to demonstrate a systematic approach to educational quality management.

title: BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 - Schedule structure
content: The BIS (Conformity Assessment) Regulations, 2018 organize BIS's certification activity into numbered Schemes set out in schedules - Scheme-I (general product certification/ISI mark, including the FMCS route for foreign manufacturers), Scheme-II (Compulsory Registration Scheme for electronics/IT goods), Scheme-IV, and Scheme-X (certification under the Omnibus Technical Regulation) - each schedule prescribing the specific procedural steps, forms, and timelines applicable to that certification route.

title: Appeal route - Director General followed by Central Government
content: Under Section 34 of the BIS Act, 2016, a person aggrieved by certain BIS orders (such as refusal, suspension, or cancellation of a licence) may first appeal to the Director General of BIS; a further appeal against specified categories of order may then lie to the Central Government department with administrative control of BIS (currently the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution), providing a two-tier appellate structure within the certification and hallmarking framework.

title: Grouping of product varieties under a single BIS licence
content: A single BIS product-certification licence can cover multiple varieties, sizes, or grades of a product manufactured by the same licensee, grouped together per the 'grouping guidelines' set out in the product's Product Manual - reducing the need for the manufacturer to hold separate licences for each individual size/grade combination, provided the varieties share sufficiently similar manufacturing and testing characteristics.

title: BIS licence validity - typical initial period and renewal cycle
content: A BIS product certification licence under Scheme-I is typically granted for an initial period of up to two years after payment of the advance minimum marking fee, and may thereafter be renewed for periods of up to five years at a time from the last date of validity, upon submission of the requisite renewal application, fee, and supporting documents.

title: Timely submission of renewal applications
content: Licensees are advised to submit their BIS licence-renewal application with the requisite fee and documents well before the expiry of the current licence validity period, since a lapse in an active, valid licence can interrupt a manufacturer's ability to legally use the Standard Mark on QCO-covered products during the gap.

title: Marking-fee concessions for MSMEs, startups, and women entrepreneurs
content: BIS provides concessions in marking fees for micro units, startups, and women entrepreneurs in certain product categories (such as toys), as part of its broader effort to reduce the compliance cost of certification for smaller manufacturers while still requiring conformity with the applicable Indian Standard.
source_name: Bureau of Indian Standards (via Ministry of Consumer Affairs)

title: Certification pathway comparison for domestic vs foreign manufacturers
content: Domestic manufacturers apply for BIS product certification directly under Scheme-I via manakonline.in; foreign manufacturers of the same general product category apply through the Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS), except where the product falls under Electronics/IT goods, in which case both domestic and foreign manufacturers instead use the Compulsory Registration Scheme (CRS) via crsbis.in - so the applicable route depends jointly on the manufacturer's location and the product's category.

title: BIS Care app - product recall feature
content: BIS has extended the BIS Care app with a product-recall-related feature (recorded in app release notes as a 'ProdRecallViewModel' update supporting new API changes), enabling the app to surface product-recall information to consumers alongside its existing licence/HUID/registration verification and complaint-lodging functions.

title: e-BIS integrated portal - Standardization, Conformity Assessment and Training
content: BIS operates an integrated e-BIS platform covering its core functions - the Standardization Portal, the Conformity Assessment Portal (manakonline.in), and the Training Portal - launched together with the BIS Care mobile app on 28 July 2020 by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, aimed at digitizing and integrating manufacturer, jeweller, laboratory, and consumer interactions with BIS.

title: BIS certification and India's Make in India / import-substitution policy
content: BIS's product-certification and QCO framework supports India's broader Make in India and import-substitution policy objectives by ensuring both domestically manufactured and imported goods in covered categories meet the same Indian Standards, aiming to prevent an influx of substandard imported products from undercutting quality-compliant domestic manufacturers while promoting export competitiveness for BIS-certified Indian products.

title: Technical-department consultation before issuance of a QCO
content: Before a line ministry issues a Quality Control Order for a product, it consults with BIS - typically through the technical department responsible for the relevant Indian Standard - to confirm the standard is technically finalized, that testing infrastructure (BIS labs, recognized labs) is adequate to support the resulting certification demand, and to align the QCO's product scope with the standard's defined scope.

title: Cement - long-standing mandatory BIS certification category
content: Cement (covered by standards including IS 269 for Ordinary Portland Cement, IS 1489 for Portland Pozzolana Cement, and IS 12269 for 53-grade OPC) has long been one of the core categories under compulsory BIS certification, reflecting cement's structural-safety significance in Indian construction and its status as one of the earliest and most consistently enforced QCO-covered product families.

title: Textile QCO family - medical textiles, agro textiles, and viscose staple fibre
content: Beyond woven-sack packaging, BIS's textile-sector Quality Control Orders have also covered categories such as Medical Textiles (Quality Control) Order, 2023 (effective 1 April 2024) and Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order, 2023 (effective 1 April 2024); a related Viscose Staple Fibres (Quality Control) Order, 2022 was later withdrawn by the Ministry of Textiles on 18 November 2025 in the public interest, after consultation with BIS.
